description: Researched checklist data proposed for merge into the knowledge base. Not yet merged.
scope: The 40 highest-capacity programmes across northstar/data/programmes.json and programmes_extracted.json (capacity 1000 down to 285), covering 17 institutions.
method: Programmes ranked by the `capacity` field across both knowledge-base files, then grouped by institution. For each institution the fee figure was taken only from a document published by that institution itself: an official fee-structure PDF, a joining-instruction PDF, an official prospectus, or the fee table on the institution's own website. PDFs were read directly (text layer, or page images where the PDF was a scan). Aggregator and SEO sites (mabumbe, eduloaded, applyscholars, wazaelimu, darasahuru, studocu, unirank, unipage, etc.) were used ONLY to locate candidate URLs and were never used as a fee source; several of them carried figures that the official documents contradicted. Where an institution's own site could not be reached or carried no fee figure, `cost` is null. `what_is_it` is written from general knowledge of the discipline and makes no Tanzania-specific salary or employment claim.

cost_field_notes.amount_tzs: Tuition only, for Tanzanian/local students. It excludes examination, registration, TCU/NACTVET quality-assurance, student-union, NHIF, accommodation, meals and book allowances, which most of these institutions bill separately. Total payable is meaningfully higher than tuition at every institution here.
cost_field_notes.basis: 'per_year' = the source states this amount as tuition for one year of study. 'total_programme' = the source states this amount as tuition for the whole programme (used for the Open University of Tanzania, which prices per unit rather than per year).
cost_field_notes.year: The academic year the source document states. Where the source carries no academic year, this is recorded explicitly as 'not stated on source' plus the retrieval date, rather than being guessed.
cost_field_notes.source_url: Page or document that carries the figure. `document_url` is given additionally where the figure lives in a PDF linked from that page.

open_flags_for_a_human: Seven institutions publish a fee figure with no academic year attached to it: TEKU, SJUT, IFM, ARU and UDSM. These are recorded as 'not stated on source' plus the retrieval date rather than assumed to be 2025/26. If the UI is going to render a year next to the number, these five need confirming with the institution first.

SUA's published undergraduate fee schedule is the one approved in March 2019. It is what SUA links from its live fees page today, but a seven-year-old figure should be confirmed before a student plans around it.

OUT does not price by year at all — it charges per unit, and the prospectus quotes a whole-programme tuition total. Any UI that renders cost as 'per year' will misrepresent OUT's nine programmes unless it reads the `basis` field.
UoI publishes tuition only as a 3-year total; the per-year figure in this file is that total divided by three, and is marked as derived.
IF006 is 'Bachelor of Science in Tax Management' in the guidebook but 'Bachelor of Science in Taxation' on IFM's fee page. Same-programme match is by inference, not by a stated equivalence.

OU020's stored name is truncated to 'Bachelor of Business Administration in Human'. The OUT 2025/2026 prospectus gives it as 'Bachelor of Business Administration in Human Resource Management' — a free correction to the knowledge base.

MK002 (TUMA) and UI002 (UoI) are Bachelor of Laws recorded at 3 years, and both institutions' own fee sheets are indeed built around a 3-year LLB — consistent, but worth noting since 4-year LLBs are common elsewhere.

Every amount here is tuition only. Administrative fees, NHIF medical capitation (typically 50,400), accommodation, meals and books are billed separately and are a large share of what a student actually pays. Showing tuition alone as 'what it costs' would understate the real figure at every one of these institutions.
